messages:
Sana R.: heads-up — we need to decide between access-graph tiling and the hybrid-funnel approach for console query routing. this impacts RBAC enforcement, dashboard latency, and cacheability. thoughts?
Liam M.: can you summarize the concrete difference you care about? is this about where auth is checked (edge vs tile) or about how many fanouts we do?
Sana R.: both. access-graph tiling = precompute per-tenant tiles with permissions applied. hybrid-funnel = keep coarse tiles + auth at the query edge, with selective re-materialization for high-cardinality tenants. tradeoffs: storage + materialization time vs per-request fanout & auth checks.
Priya S.: short list of constraints: 1) 95th p99 latency target for dashboard render 150ms, 2) cost cap for dedicated pools, 3) preserve ability to do canary rollouts per-tenant.
Josh T.: hybrid-funnel seems attractive for low-cardinality tenants (cheap) but worst-case fanout explosion for large customers. how often do we see these large-cardinality queries? infra-bot: metric: top-10 tenants account for ~62% of dashboard tile rows over last 30d.
Liam M.: sounds like we need a split strategy: precompute tiles for heavy tenants (tiling) and funnel for the rest. but that adds complexity in ownership/infra.
Sana R.: exactly — proposal: "tiling-first with funnel fallback". serve from tile if tenant is on tiling registry; otherwise route through funnel auth edge that can short-circuit using prefix-cache. fallback rules: if funnel exceeds N fanout or latency threshold, queue a background materialization job.
Priya S.: queued background materialization + graceful stale response is fine. but we need clear SLOs: e.g., on first cold request trigger materialize, mark cache-stale and serve degraded UI with a banner. ops needs runbooks.
Josh T.: devops note — materialization jobs need priority and resource isolation. otherwise a sudden re-materialization storm could thrash GPUs/CPUs. we should rate-limit and use token-bucket per-tenant.
Liam M.: RBAC surface: where do we evaluate row-level permissions? if we precompute tiles, we bake effective-ACL into tile. for funnel, we must enforce at read time. mixing these must ensure equivalence. also need signed tile manifests to avoid stale-perm leaks.
Sana R.: agreed on signed manifests + TTL + revocation queue. revocation path: when permission change occurs, push an invalidate for that tenant's tiles + optionally increment tile-version to force funnel reads.
Priya S.: performance tradeoff: tiling reduces per-request auth checks but increases storage and stale window. hybrid keeps storage small but increases per-request CPU. also caching patterns differ. we should quantify break-even point: projection rows per tenant vs tile materialization cost.
Josh T.: can we instrument a sampling job to simulate both strategies? e.g., replay last 30d traffic and model cost/latency for both. infra-bot: scheduled job created: simulate-access-graph-tiling-vs-funnel (ETA 3d).
Liam M.: implementation sketch: 1) tiling-registry service + assigner 2) funnel-router in query edge with auth adapter 3) materializer service with backoff + priority lanes 4) tile storage + signed manifests 5) metrics/alerts: fanout, tile-hit-rate, materialization-queue-depth, stale-serves.
Sana R.: action items: Priya to own SLO language + UX degrade copy, Liam to draft RFC for registry & manifest signing, Josh to prototype token-bucket materializer throttling, infra-bot to run the simulation and post results. sync Friday 10am.
Priya S.: +1 — will add runbook snippet for manual tile invalidation.
Josh T.: will sketch k8s job templates for materializers and throttling knobs.
Liam M.: one more: consider multi-tenant tiles vs tenant-isolated depending on privacy. some enterprise customers will require tenant-isolated storage (private). note that doubles storage cost but required for Private deployments.
Sana R.: good call — include privacy flag in tiling-registry and propagate to storage policy. thanks all. :thumbsup:
